literal_edits.before: 1.2 The defining relations of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ hold on $V$; equivalently $V$ is a $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module. Toral conjugation: $K_hE_iK_h^{-1}v_j$ has coefficient $q^{\langle\lambda_j,h\rangle}q^{\langle\lambda_{j-1}-\lambda_j,h\rangle}=q^{\langle\alpha_{j-1},h\rangle}$ on $v_{j-1}$ whenever $j\equiv i+1$, and $\alpha_{j-1}=\alpha_i$ then, so $K_hE_iK_h^{-1}=q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_i$; similarly $K_hF_iK_h^{-1}=q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_i$. Mixed commutators: for $i\ne j$, both $F_jE_i$ and $E_iF_j$ contain successive shifts by residues $i+1$ then $j$, and $i+1\equiv j$ would give $i\equiv j$, so both compositions vanish; for $i=j$, $E_iF_iv_j=\delta_{j\equiv i}v_j$ and $F_iE_iv_j=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}v_j$, while $(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q-q^{-1})v_j=\frac{q^{\delta_{ij}-\delta_{i,j-1}}-q^{-\delta_{ij}+\delta_{i,j-1}}}{q-q^{-1}}v_j$, which is $1$ for $j\equiv i$, $-1$ for $j\equiv i+1$ and $0$ otherwise; the two sides agree. Serre sums: $E_i^2=0$ and $F_i^2=0$ for every $i$, because $E_i^2v_j\ne0$ would need $j\equiv i+1$ and $j-1\equiv i+1$, that is $i\equiv i+1$ in $\mathbb Z/e\mathbb Z$, impossible for $e\ge2$; every Serre summand contains $E_i^{1-a_{ij}}$ or $F_i^{1-a_{ij}}$ with $1-a_{ij}\ge2$, so all Serre sums vanish. Hence the universal property [F1] gives the module structure, and linearity is clear. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]
literal_edits.after: 1.2 The derived defining relations hold on $V$. For $h\in P^\vee_{\mathrm{cl}}$ and $j\equiv i+1$, conjugation gives $K_hE_iK_h^{-1}v_j=q^{\langle\lambda_{j-1}-\lambda_j,h\rangle}v_{j-1}$ with cyclic representatives; the weight difference is $\alpha_i$ for $j\ge2$ and $\alpha_0-\delta$ for $j=1$, and $\langle\delta,h\rangle=0$, so the coefficient is $q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}$ in both cases. Reversing the arrow gives $K_hF_iK_h^{-1}=q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_i$. For distinct colors $i,t$, $E_iF_tv_j$ can be nonzero only if $j\equiv t$ and $j+1\equiv i+1$, which forces $t=i$; $F_tE_iv_j$ can be nonzero only if $j\equiv i+1$ and $j-1\equiv t$, again forcing $t=i$, so both vanish when $t\ne i$. For equal colors, $E_iF_iv_j=\delta_{j\equiv i}v_j$ and $F_iE_iv_j=\delta_{j\equiv i+1}v_j$, and $K_iv_j=q^{\delta_{i,j}-\delta_{i,j-1}}v_j$; thus $(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q-q^{-1})$ acts by $1,-1,0$ respectively when $j\equiv i$, $j\equiv i+1$, or neither. Finally $E_i^2=F_i^2=0$ because two successive steps of one color would require $i\equiv i+1$. For $e\ge3$ and $a_{it}=0$, $E_iE_t$ requires $t=i+1$ and $E_tE_i$ requires $t=i-1$, both excluded by nonadjacency; the corresponding $F$ paths require $t=i-1$ or $t=i+1$ and also vanish. For $a_{it}=-1$, the outside terms of $E_i^2E_t-(q+q^{-1})E_iE_tE_i+E_tE_i^2$ vanish by $E_i^2=0$; its middle path would require, from right to left, residues $i+1\to i\to i-1$ and then $i-1\equiv i+1$, impossible for $e\ge3$. The middle $F_iF_tF_i$ path requires $i\to i+1\to i+2$ and then $i+2\equiv i$, also impossible. For $e=2$, $a_{it}=-2$ and every cubic Serre term $E_i^{3-r}E_tE_i^r$ ($0\le r\le3$) has at least one side exponent at least $2$, so it vanishes; the same holds for $F$. These arguments check all derived relations, including the double edge. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

literal_edits.before: 2.1 $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ is a $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module with the stated weights and integrable strings. The toral conjugation checks of step 1.2 transfer verbatim because $E_i$ and $F_i$ move one residue in the same direction and the $K$-eigenvalues record the weights; explicitly, $E_iu_m\ne0$ shifts the weight by $\mathrm{wt}(u_{m-1})-\mathrm{wt}(u_m)=\alpha_i$ when $m\equiv i+1$, by [F3] in the non-wrap case $j(m)\ge2$ and by $\lambda_1+\delta-\lambda_e=\alpha_0$ in the wrap case, and $F_i$ shifts by $-\alpha_i$; hence toral, mixed and Serre relations hold exactly as in step 1.2, with $E_i^2=F_i^2=0$ on $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ by the same residue argument, and $K_du_m=q^{a(m)}u_m$ by [F6]. Integrability: for fixed $i$ and $m$, the space spanned by $u_m$ together with its images under $E_i,F_i$ is $\{u_{m-1},u_m\}$ when $m\equiv i+1$, $\{u_m,u_{m+1}\}$ when $m\equiv i$, and $\{u_m\}$ otherwise, a finite-dimensional $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)_i$-stable space on which $K_i$ has the two distinct eigenvalues $q^{\pm1}$ and on which $E_i,F_i$ interchange the pair; so every $u_m$ lies in a finite-dimensional $\{E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}\}$-stable space, and $V_{\mathrm{aff}}=\bigoplus_m\mathbb Q(q)u_m$ is a weight decomposition with weights $\lambda_{j(m)}+a(m)\delta$ of level $0$. [step 1.2, step 1.3, F1, F3, F4, F6, algebra]
literal_edits.after: 2.1 $V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ is a full $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module with the stated weights and integrable strings. If $E_iu_m\ne0$, then $\mathrm{wt}(u_{m-1})-\mathrm{wt}(u_m)=\alpha_i$: for $j(m)\ge2$ this is $\lambda_{j(m)-1}-\lambda_{j(m)}$; for $j(m)=1$ the new pair is $(e,a(m)+1)$, giving $\lambda_e+\delta-\lambda_1=\alpha_0$ by [F3]. Reversing these arrows gives weight difference $-\alpha_i$ for $F_i$. Hence the full toral conjugation relations hold for every $h\in P^\vee$, and the additive weight pairing gives $K_0=1$ and $K_hK_{h'}=K_{h+h'}$. The mixed and Serre computations of step 1.2 apply to the same integer residue paths on $u_m$; when a same-color mixed composition is nonzero, its two opposite steps return to $u_m$, so their coefficients and the $K_i$ commutator are unchanged. Thus [F1] gives the full module structure, and $K_du_m=q^{a(m)}u_m$ by [F6]. Each color acts on disjoint pairs $\{u_{i+ke},u_{i+ke+1}\}$ with $K_i$ eigenvalues $q,q^{-1}$ and one-step raising and lowering maps, and on singleton vectors of other residues with $K_i$ eigenvalue $1$ and both maps zero. Every basis vector therefore lies in a finite-dimensional rank-one stable space, so the module is integrable and its displayed weight decomposition has level $0$. Finally multiplication by $z$ commutes with $E_i,F_i$ and every derived $K_h$, since $\langle\delta,h\rangle=0$ there. The subspace $(z-1)V_{\mathrm{aff}}$ is consequently stable under the genuine subalgebra $U_q'(\mathfrak g)$, and its quotient, identified with $V$ by $z^av_j\mapsto v_j$, carries exactly the finite operators of step 1.2. This proves the claimed derived module action without assigning $K_d$ to finite $V$. [step 1.2, step 1.3, F1, F2, F3, F4, F6, algebra]

literal_edits.before: 4.1 The tensor rule $\otimes_+$ together with $\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i$ is a legitimate crystal rule on $B_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes B_{\mathrm{aff}}$, and it is the opposite-coproduct $\otimes_+$ rule of the cited KMPY section. The assignments $f_i$, $e_i$ of the definition are partial maps with images in $B_{\mathrm{aff}}$, and for all $x,y$ one has $\varepsilon_i(x\otimes y)=\max(\varepsilon_i(x)-\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(y)\rangle,\varepsilon_i(y))$ and $\varphi_i(x\otimes y)=\max(\varphi_i(x),\varphi_i(y)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(x)\rangle)$: for the first identity, if $\varepsilon_i(x)\ge\varphi_i(y)$ then $f_i(x\otimes y)=f_ix\otimes y$ and computing $\varphi_i$ of the tensor from the rule gives $\varphi_i(x\otimes y)=\max(\varphi_i(x),\varphi_i(y)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(x)\rangle)$, so subtracting $\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(x)+\mathrm{wt}(y)\rangle$ and using $\varphi_i=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$ on each factor yields $\max(\varepsilon_i(x)-\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(y)\rangle,\varepsilon_i(y))$; the case $\varepsilon_i(x)<\varphi_i(y)$ is symmetric, and the same computation in reverse gives the second identity. Consequently $\varphi_i(x\otimes y)=\varepsilon_i(x\otimes y)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(x\otimes y)\rangle$, the weight of a tensor is additive, and the two maps $f_i,e_i$ are the partial inverses prescribed by that rule. [step 3.1, given, algebra]
literal_edits.after: 4.1 The opposite-channel tensor rule is a crystal rule on $B_{\mathrm{aff}}\otimes B_{\mathrm{aff}}$. For one fixed color write $+$ for a top vector with $(\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i)=(0,1)$, $-$ for its bottom vector with $(1,0)$, and $o$ for a singleton with $(0,0)$. The displayed rule gives exactly the strings $++\xrightarrow{f_i}+-\xrightarrow{f_i}--$, $+o\xrightarrow{f_i}-o$, and $o+\xrightarrow{f_i}o-$, with $-+$ and $oo$ isolated; the displayed $e_i$ reverses each arrow, including the ties. Thus the string lengths $(\varepsilon_i,\varphi_i)$ are respectively $(0,2),(1,1),(2,0)$ on the first string, $(0,1),(1,0)$ on the next two strings, and $(0,0)$ on the isolated pairs. These nine cases give $\varepsilon_i(x\otimes y)=\max(\varepsilon_i(x)-\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(y)\rangle,\varepsilon_i(y))$ and $\varphi_i(x\otimes y)=\max(\varphi_i(x),\varphi_i(y)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(x)\rangle)$, using step 3.1 on the factors. They imply $\varphi_i-\varepsilon_i=\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(x)+\mathrm{wt}(y)\rangle$; each arrow changes the additive weight by $-\alpha_i$ and its inverse by $\alpha_i$. This verifies the claimed rule, which is the opposite-coproduct $\otimes_+$ rule in the cited KMPY section. [step 2.1, step 3.1, given, algebra]
